# dbt_marketing/models/staging/_sources.yml (80 lines)
version: 2

sources:
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Observable data. Everything downstream may read these.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  - name: raw
    description: >
      Data as it arrived, written by attribution/ingest.py. Never edited in
      place - it is reproducible from the Kaggle CSV plus the seeded generator.
    schema: raw
    tables:
      - name: touchpoints
        description: One row per marketing exposure. The observable journey.

        # Freshness against the dataset's own clock, not the wall clock. The
        # generator writes fixed dates (2026-01-01 to 2026-04-13), so
        # comparing max(touched_at) to now() would fail forever on clean data.
        # loaded_at_query returns "now, minus how far max(touched_at) sits
        # behind data_as_of", which makes the age equal to
        # data_as_of - max(touched_at): about a day on clean data, and 30 days
        # if a load ever lands with backdated timestamps.
        loaded_at_query: |
          select cast(current_timestamp as timestamp)
                 - (cast('{{ var("data_as_of") }}' as timestamp) - max(touched_at))
          from {{ this }}
        freshness:
          warn_after: {count: 2, period: day}
          error_after: {count: 7, period: day}
        columns:
          - name: user_id
            description: Synthetic user identifier.
          - name: touch_number
            description: 0-based position of this touch within the user's journey.
          - name: touched_at
            description: When the exposure happened.
          - name: channel
            description: Marketing channel (six values, see channels.py).
          - name: campaign
            description: Campaign within the channel, three per channel.
          - name: cost
            description: What we paid for this touch, USD. Organic and direct are free.

      - name: conversions
        description: One row per user, whether or not they converted.
        columns:
          - name: user_id
          - name: converted
          - name: journey_length
            description: >
              Touch count as recorded by the generator. We deliberately recount
              it from touchpoints in int_journeys and test that the two agree -
              see tests/assert_journey_length_reconciles.sql.
          - name: converted_at
          - name: revenue

      - name: kaggle_ads
        description: >
          Real Facebook ad performance, 1,143 rows of ad-level aggregates. Used
          only to calibrate the generator; it has no user IDs so it cannot
          support attribution itself.

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # ANSWER KEY. Declared so it is documented and so the leakage test can name
  # it - NOT so it can be used. No model may depend on these tables.
  # tests/assert_no_answer_key_leakage.sql enforces this at build time.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  - name: answer_key
    description: >
      GROUND TRUTH - which touch actually caused each conversion, and the lift
      parameters we planted. Reading these from any staging, intermediate or
      marts model is target leakage: attribution models would score perfectly
      and mean nothing. Phase 4 is the only consumer, and it reads them
      directly rather than through dbt.
    schema: raw
    tables:
      - name: true_effects
        description: Per-touch record of whether that touch fired the conversion.
      - name: channel_ground_truth
        description: The planted per-channel conversion_lift.

# dbt_marketing/dbt_project.yml (67 lines)
name: "marketing_attribution"
version: "2.0.0"
config-version: 2

profile: "marketing_attribution"

model-paths: ["models"]
macro-paths: ["macros"]
test-paths: ["tests"]
target-path: "target"
clean-targets: ["target", "dbt_packages"]

flags:
  send_anonymous_usage_stats: false

vars:
  # How long a gap between two touches starts a new session.
  #
  # The web-analytics default is 30 minutes, inherited from Google Analytics.
  # That default assumes clickstream data - many events per visit, minutes
  # apart. Our touchpoints are cross-channel marketing exposures with a mean
  # gap of 3.5 days, so a 30-minute rule would put nearly every touch in its
  # own session and the session layer would carry no information.
  #
  # 1440 minutes (24h) groups same-day multi-channel activity, which is the
  # thing worth grouping here. Change it and re-run to see the grain move:
  #   dbt build --vars 'session_gap_minutes: 30'
  session_gap_minutes: 1440

  # Half-life for the time-decay attribution model, in days: a touch this many
  # days before the conversion carries half the weight of a touch at the moment
  # of conversion.
  #
  # 7 days is the industry default, inherited from Google Ads. It is almost
  # certainly WRONG for this data, and that is deliberate - see the note in
  # int_attribution_weights.sql. Phase 2 established that defaults encode
  # assumptions about data that isn't yours (the 30-minute session gap), and
  # this is the same lesson with a knob attached. Sweep it:
  #   dbt build --vars 'time_decay_half_life_days: 30'
  time_decay_half_life_days: 7

  # The dataset's "today". The generator writes fixed dates, so source
  # freshness (models/staging/_sources.yml) measures age against this instead
  # of the wall clock. Move it forward if the raw layer is regenerated.
  data_as_of: '2026-04-14'

  # Days from the first touch during which new journeys are still being
  # started. generate.py draws journey_starts from uniform(0, window_days * 0.6)
  # with window_days = 90, so daily volume is steady for 54 days and then decays
  # as journeys finish. tests/assert_daily_touchpoint_volume.sql only judges
  # the steady window; a decay is not a drop.
  touchpoint_volume_window_days: 54

models:
  marketing_attribution:
    staging:
      +materialized: view
      +schema: staging
    intermediate:
      # Intermediate models land in `staging` rather than a schema of their own
      # so the database keeps the three-layer story (raw / staging / marts)
      # described in the README. The `int_` prefix keeps them distinguishable.
      +materialized: view
      +schema: staging
    marts:
      +materialized: table
      +schema: marts

diff --git a/dbt_marketing/tests/assert_daily_touchpoint_volume.sql b/dbt_marketing/tests/assert_daily_touchpoint_volume.sql
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..7014dc1
--- /dev/null
+++ b/dbt_marketing/tests/assert_daily_touchpoint_volume.sql
@@ -0,0 +1,70 @@
+{#- One parent, so dagster-dbt turns this into an asset check on
+    stg_touchpoints without a meta hint (see assert_touches_precede_conversion
+    for the multi-parent case). -#}
+
+-- Volume drop detection. A day whose touchpoint count is below half the
+-- median of the seven days before it is a failure. Half the trailing median is
+-- deliberately loose: normal day-to-day noise here is well under 20%, so this
+-- only fires when a chunk of a day is missing, which is what a partial load or
+-- a truncated export looks like.
+--
+-- Scoped to the steady-state window. generate.py starts new journeys for the
+-- first window_days * 0.6 = 54 days and then only finishes existing ones, so
+-- volume decays by design from day 55 onwards. Judging that decay would fail
+-- on clean data, so the window is a var (touchpoint_volume_window_days) and
+-- the test stops at the end of it. The first seven days are skipped because a
+-- trailing median needs seven prior days to mean anything.
+
+with daily as (
+
+    select
+        cast(touched_at as date) as touch_date,
+        count(*)                 as touch_count
+    from {{ ref('stg_touchpoints') }}
+    group by 1
+
+),
+
+steady_window as (
+
+    select
+        min(touch_date) + interval {{ var('touchpoint_volume_window_days') }} day
+            as ends_before
+    from daily
+
+),
+
+with_trailing as (
+
+    select
+        touch_date,
+        touch_count,
+
+        median(touch_count) over (
+            order by touch_date
+            rows between 7 preceding and 1 preceding
+        ) as trailing_median,
+
+        count(*) over (
+            order by touch_date
+            rows between 7 preceding and 1 preceding
+        ) as trailing_days
+
+    from daily
+
+)
+
+select
+    t.touch_date,
+    t.touch_count,
+    t.trailing_median,
+    round(100.0 * t.touch_count / t.trailing_median, 1) as pct_of_trailing_median
+
+from with_trailing t
+cross join steady_window w
+
+where t.touch_date < w.ends_before
+  and t.trailing_days = 7
+  and t.touch_count < 0.5 * t.trailing_median
+
+order by t.touch_date
